title: Understanding Structural Shifts in Global Trade and Supply Chains
subtitle: Why the hyperglobalization era ended, how the new trade order is being built, and what it means for Indian markets
description: An advanced framework for macro-focused investors, fund managers, and senior finance professionals on the structural realignment of global trade and supply chains. Covers the end of hyperglobalization and its fracture points (2008, the US-China trade war, COVID, Russia-Ukraine), the new toolkit of economic statecraft (tariffs, sanctions, export controls, industrial policy), the leading indicators that signal supply chain stress before it hits earnings, the great manufacturing realignment across ASEAN, Mexico, and semiconductors, India's specific position as a China+1 beneficiary with its own import vulnerabilities, and a forward-looking scenario framework for translating these shifts into sector and portfolio decisions. Anchored throughout in Indian context: PLI schemes, NSE and BSE sector performance, RBI and commerce ministry data, and real episodes from the last two decades of trade realignment.
topics: India's PLI Schemes and Sectoral Winners
whatYouLearn: Explain why the hyperglobalization era broke down, from the 2008 crisis through COVID and the Russia-Ukraine shock
Understand tariffs, sanctions, export controls and industrial policy as tools of economic statecraft, and how markets price them
Read supply chain stress before it hits earnings, using shipping rates, PMI new orders and inventory-to-sales data
Trace the China+1 realignment of manufacturing across ASEAN, Mexico and the semiconductor industry
Identify India's sectoral winners and vulnerabilities in the new trade order, from PLI beneficiaries to import-dependent sectors
Build a scenario framework for fragmentation, reglobalization or bloc formation, and translate it into portfolio decisions
